messages.subject: Re: dcast creates margin colname with parentheses
messages.subject_clean: dcast creates margin colname with parentheses
messages.body_plain:
On Mar 29, 2013, at 2:40 AM, Duncan McPherson wrote:

> Thanks for the great package, I'm just learning R and reshape2, and have come across a problem I can't obviously see an answer to:
>
> I've got a data frame in molten format, and then using cast() on it. I've got margins=TRUE so I get totals back, but the column name for the totals is (all).
>
> I then feed these into another function, which renames the column since there is some sort of special-ness about using parentheses in column names as is outlined here:
> http://stackoverflow.com/questions/14624736/r-changing-column-names-containing-plus-or-brackets
>
> The problem is I want to create a function that automatically processes these new data frames, but it needs to know what the column name is.
>
> Is there a way of either preventing the parentheses being inserted in the first place, or predicting what the renamed column will be called?
>
> An example is:
>
> > demog.samp
>       sex br_age count
> 1  female  70-79  1124
> 2    male  60-69     1
> 3  female    80+    36
> 4    male    80+     1
> 5    male  20-49     3
> 6  female  70-79    23
> 7  female  60-69     1
> 8  female  60-69     2
> 9    male  60-69     1
> 10   male  60-69    93
> 11 female  70-79     9
> 12   male  20-49     5
> 13   male    80+     5
> 14   male  20-49     1
> 15 female  20-49     8
> 16   male  20-49     1
> 17 female  50-59     1
> 18 female  60-69     1
> 19   male  60-69    19
> 20 female  70-79   302
> > cast.demog.samp<-dcast(demog.samp, br_age~sex, fun.aggregate=sum, value.var="count", margins=TRUE)
> >
>   br_age female male (all)
> 1  20-49      8   10    18
> 2  50-59      1    0     1
> 3  60-69      4  114   118
> 4  70-79   1458    0  1458
> 5    80+     36    6    42
> 6  (all)   1507  130  1637
> > est.cast.demog.samp<- transform(cast.demog.samp, f.est=binom.confint(cast.demog.samp$female, cast.demog.samp$"(all)", methods="agresti-coull")$mean)
> > est.cast.demog.samp
>   br_age female male X.all.      f.est
> 1  20-49      8   10     18 0.44444444
> 2  50-59      1    0      1 1.00000000
> 3  60-69      4  114    118 0.03389831
> 4  70-79   1458    0   1458 1.00000000
> 5    80+     36    6     42 0.85714286
> 6  (all)   1507  130   1637 0.92058644
>
> You'll see that the column that was "(all)" is now called "X.all.".
>
> Is there a reason for using parentheses, or can the column be called something else that doesn't induce later renaming? Can I control this naming myself?

I can think of no reason why a column name should be returned as a value that will not pass check.names(). You can see what it will be converted to by check.names (X.all) and there's a fairly high degree of confidence that if you used:

 names( cast.demog.samp) <- check.names(names( cast.demog.samp) )

... that you would get the "(all)" converted to "X.all". My constructive suggestion would be to return a dataframe from `dcast` with an ALL-column named "_all_" but that decision remains with Hadley.

If you wanted to change your installations behavior I think I have identified where in the code tree the naming is occurring:

> add_margins
function (df, vars, margins = TRUE)
{
    margin_vars <- margins(vars, margins)
    if (length(margin_vars) == 0)
        return(df)
    addAll <- function(x) {
        x <- addNA(x, TRUE)
        factor(x, levels = c(levels(x), "(all)"), exclude = NULL)
    }
    vars <- unique(unlist(margin_vars))
    df[vars] <- lapply(df[vars], addAll)
    rownames(df) <- NULL
    margin_dfs <- llply(margin_vars, function(vars) {
        df[vars] <- rep(list(factor("(all)")), length(vars))
        df
    })
    rbind.fill(margin_dfs)
}
<environment: namespace:reshape2>

So you could do brain surgery on R by replacing that function in the reshape2 namespace with one that did not use illegal column names.
--

David Winsemius
Alameda, CA, USA

I can see what you're after in principle, David, but alas there is no
check.names() function:

names( cast.demog.samp) <- check.names(names( cast.demog.samp) )

Error: could not find function "check.names"

An sos search also came up empty. However, several data reading
functions have a logical check.names = argument, including
read.table() and data.table(), and it would seem prudent that such
checking take place in reshape2 and wherever else it may relevant.

However, a suggestion to use "_all_" doesn't fare any better:

I went through the read.table() function, and in the section of the
code corresponding to check.names, use was made of the base package
function make.names(), so I tried it as defined in read.table() for
this example in a fresh session under R-3.0-0 RC, Win7:

> ls()
[1] "cast.demog.samp"     "demog.samp"          "est.cast.demog.samp"
> make.names(names(cast.demog.samp), unique = TRUE)
[1] "br_age" "female" "male"   "X.all."
> names(cast.demog.samp)
[1] "br_age" "female" "male"   "(all)"
> names(cast.demog.samp)[4] <- "_all_"
> names(cast.demog.samp)
[1] "br_age" "female" "male"   "_all_"
> make.names(names(cast.demog.samp), unique = TRUE)
[1] "br_age" "female" "male"   "X_all_"

In that context, it seems safer to use a word for the row/column
margin of a [da]cast() table, or at least one that starts with a
letter; just as a test,

> names(cast.demog.samp)[4] <- "all_"
> make.names(names(cast.demog.samp), unique = TRUE)
[1] "br_age" "female" "male"   "all_"

Several possibilities for margin names spring to mind, including the
function name if fun.aggregate is supplied, but that can be left to
the package maintainers.

Hadley, should this be filed as an issue?

Dennis

I'm sorry... I was conflating the name of the read.table parameter with the function that gets called by read.table:

check.names
logical. If TRUE then the names of the variables in the data frame are checked to ensure that they are syntactically valid variable names. If necessary they are adjusted (by make.names) so that they are, and also to ensure that there are no duplicates.

The function name is `make.names`.

--

Thank you for your ideas. In summary it seems that my choices are either to add an extra step to deliberately rename the (all) column to something else I choose before further processing it, or to rely on the inbuilt renaming rules being consistent, or to do brain surgery.

I'm going to have to do this a fair bit, so remembering to re-name the column every time is bound to fail.

The inbuilt rules seem to be to swap parentheses to dots, which still produces as illegal colname, so then add a X to make it start with a letter. Hopefully I've got the right idea here, but you never know.

Now, I'm only an anaesthetist (anesthesiologist on your side of the pond), so I don't know much about brain surgery, but I know it's not rocket science ;-)

Helpfully you've given me the add_margins() function, so all I have to do is figure out how to use it. Since yesterday I've come across another example of this problem, and, using your advice, seem to have (temporarily) solved it:

> mutate(cast.demog.samp, perc.female=female*100)
  br_age female male (all) perc.female
1  20-49      0   79    79           0
2  50-59      3  131   134         300
3  60-69      7  231   238         700
4  70-79      8    8    16         800
5    80+      0   95    95           0
6  (all)     18  544   562        1800
> mutate(cast.demog.samp, perc.female=female*100/(all))
Error in female * 100/(all) : non-numeric argument to binary operator
> mutate(cast.demog.samp, perc.female=female*100/"(all)")
Error in female * 100/"(all)" : non-numeric argument to binary operator
> mutate(cast.demog.samp, perc.female=female*100/"\(all\)")
Error: '\(' is an unrecognized escape in character string starting "\("
> mutate(cast.demog.samp, perc.female=female*100/\(all\))
Error: unexpected input in "mutate(cast.demog.samp, perc.female=female*100/\"
> mutate(cast.demog.samp, perc.female=female*100/quote((all)))
Error in female * 100/quote((all)) :
  non-numeric argument to binary operator
> mutate(cast.demog.samp, perc.female=female*100/(colnames(cast.demog.samp)[4]))
Error in female * 100/(colnames(cast.demog.samp)[4]) :
  non-numeric argument to binary operator

As you can see, lots of futile attempts to reference the "(all)". Can you figure out a way for me to reference the column name here?

I've tried a little light brain tinkering which seems to work:

So just for chuckles first do this:

library("fortunes")
fortune("brain surgery")

And do note that April 1 is almost upon us again.

OK, now your are ready for brain surgery ... it won't hurt a bit:

# First get the code from:
reshape2:::add_margins

# Then edit it very slightly, replacing "(all)" with "all_"

add_margins <- function (df, vars, margins = TRUE)

{
    margin_vars <- margins(vars, margins)
    if (length(margin_vars) == 0)
        return(df)
    addAll <- function(x) {
        x <- addNA(x, TRUE)

        factor(x, levels = c(levels(x), "all_"), exclude = NULL)
    }

    vars <- unique(unlist(margin_vars))
    df[vars] <- lapply(df[vars], addAll)
    rownames(df) <- NULL
    margin_dfs <- llply(margin_vars, function(vars) {
        df[vars] <- rep(list(factor("(all)")), length(vars))
        df
    })
    rbind.fill(margin_dfs)
}

assignInNamespace('add_margins', add_margins, ns='reshape2')

# You can see the effect took hold by checking with:

reshape2:::add_margins

This will not affect your reshape2 package and restarting R will bring back the original behavior. If you want it to become persistent then you should add this to your .Rprofile file that gets loaded at startup:

?Startup

And I'm probably even less qualified than you to do brain surgery. My medical credentials are in Family Medicine.
